chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Sa'id ibn Yasar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the camel [being sold] for two camels, hand-to-hand with delay (nasi'ah). He said, 'There is no objection to it.' Then he said, 'The delay must be specified.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell one camel for two camels with delayed delivery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of exchanging one camel for two with a deferred delivery period (nasi'ah), provided the delay is explicitly stipulated. This ruling highlights the distinction between permissible deferred exchange (bay' al-nasi'ah) and the prohibition of riba (usury), emphasizing that clarity in the time of delivery prevents ambiguity and ensures fairness in trade. The hadith reflects the practical juristic approach of the Ahl al-Bayt in regulating commercial transactions to uphold economic justice.
